business_problem: Setagaya City needed to modernize a restrictive three-layer municipal security model so staff could collaborate securely, work remotely, and support a broader digital-transformation agenda.
solution_summary: Setagaya City used Azure and Microsoft 365 services to make administrative collaboration less dependent on email and phone while still respecting public-sector security constraints such as LGWAN separation and the city's alpha, beta, and beta-prime operating models. The DX Promotion Department approached the work iteratively, building a cloud communication layer first and then extending managed remote work as the security model evolved. Key components include Azure, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft 365 E5 Security, and Microsoft Intune. Setagaya City created a foundation for DX, enabled work-from-home for all employees using migrated terminals since 2023, and expects changing employee work styles to translate into better resident services.

solution_components.name: Azure
solution_components.role: provides the cloud platform on which Setagaya City built its modern communication environment

solution_components.name: Microsoft Teams
solution_components.role: serves as the primary collaboration layer that reduces reliance on email and phone calls

solution_components.name: Microsoft SharePoint
solution_components.role: supports shared information management on the city's collaboration platform

solution_components.name: Microsoft 365 E5 Security
solution_components.role: adds the security controls needed for home-based work on managed terminals

solution_components.name: Microsoft Intune
solution_components.role: manages devices used for secure remote work and endpoint expansion

data_flow: Administrative communication and shared data now move through Teams and SharePoint on Azure instead of isolated email and phone channels, while Intune-managed endpoints protected by Microsoft 365 E5 Security let employees reach those services from approved remote environments under the evolving beta-prime model.
